about: How another model's own logic was merged into Vote Helper's single set of questions and mappings. These are judgment calls made when merging (by Claude, 2026-10-30), meant to be reviewed by the other model in the critique step. tools/merge-logic.js applies this file.
label: Grok

pretrial_detention.why: Holding more people before trial is one form of the broader enforcement-vs-reform split Vote Helper already asks about; Grok's side B (detain high-risk defendants) is Vote Helper's side B (more enforcement).

criminal_justice_orientation.why: Same question: alternatives and lower incarceration (A) vs. stronger detention and prosecution (B).

local_judicial_residency.why: Same question. Vote Helper asks it only as a follow-up for Public Question 2, since it concerns one measure; both point a Yes on PQ2 toward relaxing the residency rule.

election_integrity_priority.why: Same core split: broad access and participation (A) vs. stricter verification and fraud prevention (B). Grok's side A also mentions independent oversight of the office, which Vote Helper asks as the audit follow-up.

fiscal_restraint.why: Same trade-off: more services with higher taxes (A) vs. lower taxes and spending (B).

party_governance.why: Same question, same sides. Vote Helper's wording is kept because Grok's side A groups independents with Democrats; Grok's score for the independent commissioner candidate follows that grouping and is left for the critique step.

border_immigration_enforcement.why: A disagreement Vote Helper doesn't ask about yet. Vote Helper had folded immigration enforcement into crime and justice; immigration is a separate split among voters and recurs in federal races.

new.label: Immigration
new.q: How should the federal government handle immigration?
new.a: Emphasize legal pathways and humane processing, with enforcement targeted at serious offenders
new.b: Emphasize border control, broad enforcement and limits on illegal entry

constitutional_caution.why: A disagreement Vote Helper doesn't ask about: how readily to amend the state constitution. It applies to every legislatively referred amendment, so it carries over to later elections. Worded for any state.

new.label: Changing the state constitution
new.q: How readily should voters amend the state constitution?
new.a: Very cautiously, only for clear and narrow needs
new.b: Willingly, when lawmakers and voters see a practical problem

government_transparency.why: Same question as Vote Helper's Secretary of State audit follow-up: outside audit vs. internal state review. Grok no longer maps it to any candidate.

economic_intervention.why: Grok maps only one candidate to it, and its side B bundles lower taxes and less regulation, which the taxes and regulation questions already ask. The tariff point is kept in that candidate's notes.

law_enforcement_support.why: Grok removed every mapping to it in its corrections.

experience_vs_newcomers.why: Grok removed it in its corrections; Vote Helper's experience question remains.

education_local_control.why: Grok removed it in its corrections.

pq1#0.why: Same concern: the amendment isn't limited to violent offenses.

pq1#1.why: New: the amendment would take effect on Election Day, but the law setting hearing procedures doesn't start until January 2027.

stances.why: Where a model gives every candidate in a race the same value on a question, it has no effect and is left out.
